scripts.label: Positional passer advance alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would advance a pawn that was already passed. Keep its new square in view as you compare continuations.

scripts.label: Positional isolated actual
scripts.text: This leaves an isolated pawn, with no friendly pawn on either neighboring file.

scripts.label: Positional isolated alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave an isolated pawn, with no friendly pawn on either neighboring file.

scripts.label: Positional support actual
scripts.text: This gives a piece support. A defender is now in place.

scripts.label: Positional support alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would give a piece support. A defender would then be in place.

scripts.label: Positional unsupported alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave a piece undefended. That alone would not mean the piece could be won.

scripts.label: Positional king flight actual
scripts.text: This opens a legal flight square the king did not have before. Compare the positions to see what opened the way.

scripts.label: Positional king flight alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would open a legal flight square for the king. Compare the positions to see what would open the way.

scripts.label: Positional castling actual
scripts.text: This castles the king and relocates the rook. Follow both pieces when comparing the positions.

scripts.label: Positional castling alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would castle the king and relocate the rook. Follow where both pieces would go.

scripts.label: Positional bishop pair actual
scripts.text: This capture breaks up a bishop pair. The side losing the bishop no longer has one bishop on each square color.

scripts.label: Positional bishop pair alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would capture one bishop from an opposite-colored pair, breaking up that bishop pair.

scripts.label: Positional doubled actual
scripts.text: This leaves doubled pawns in the resulting position. At least two pawns of the same color share a file.

scripts.label: Positional doubled alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave doubled pawns in the resulting position, with at least two pawns of the same color sharing a file.

scripts.label: Missed mate
scripts.text: There was a forced checkmate in the stronger continuation. This move lets that finish go.

scripts.label: Only advantage resource
scripts.text: This was the only move we found that kept the advantage. The other moves we checked were losing.

scripts.label: Immediate capture
scripts.text: The other side has an immediate capture in reply. Follow the continuation to see which piece can be taken.

scripts.label: Reply check
scripts.text: The strongest reply gives check. The continuation begins by making the king answer that threat.

scripts.label: Stronger alternative
scripts.text: The engine prefers another move here. Compare its continuation with the move that was played.

scripts.label: Evaluation loss
scripts.text: This move gives up some of the position's value compared with the engine's best continuation. Follow the reply to see how the position changes.
